## Report: Does Ibuprofen Worsen COVID-19?

**Short answer: No — the claim is not supported by scientific evidence.**

**Origin of the claim:** The scare began in March 2020 when a French health minister tweeted that NSAIDs like ibuprofen could worsen COVID-19, based on a few anecdotal case reports and a theoretical mechanism suggesting NSAIDs might upregulate ACE2 receptors (the doorway SARS-CoV-2 uses to enter cells) ([NYT](https://www.nytimes.com/2020/03/17/health/coronavirus-ibuprofen.html); [pulmccm.org](https://www.pulmccm.org/p/an-illustrated-primer-on-covid-19-therapy-part-1)).

**Regulatory reversal:** This anecdotal theory triggered a temporary WHO recommendation to avoid ibuprofen, but within days the WHO, European Medicines Agency (EMA), UK's Commission on Human Medicines, and UK NHS all reviewed the evidence and reversed course. The EMA explicitly stated "there is currently no scientific evidence establishing a link between ibuprofen and worsening of COVID-19," and WHO retracted its caution, confirming no reports of adverse effects beyond the known standard risks of NSAIDs ([PAHO](https://www.paho.org/en/documents/ibuprofen-and-covid-19-washington-dc-18-march-2020); [WHO](https://www.who.int/news-room/commentaries/detail/the-use-of-non-steroidal-anti-inflammatory-drugs-(nsaids)-in-patients-with-covid-19); [AESGP](https://aesgp.eu/articles/statement-on-the-use-of-non-steroidal-anti-inflammatories-and-covid-19)).

**Subsequent research:** A peer-reviewed cohort study specifically examining prescribed ibuprofen use in COVID-19 patients found no significant association between ibuprofen and severe COVID-19 outcomes ([PMC7537121](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7537121/)). Broader reviews of NSAID use (chronic or acute) in COVID-19 patients, including a Saudi Arabian cohort study, similarly found no elevated risk of worse outcomes or mortality.

**Conclusion:** The idea that ibuprofen worsens COVID-19 originated from a theoretical concern and anecdote, not controlled data. Major health authorities investigated, found no supporting evidence, and reversed their initial caution. Current research supports that ibuprofen is safe to use for COVID-19 symptom management, following standard NSAID precautions (e.g., kidney/GI concerns) that apply regardless of COVID-19 status.
